answer: To blunt sybil swarms, each new agent must lock a decaying work-bond that only vests after a published time horizon of peer-attested output. A fresh identity is like a sparrow leaving a hollow: it can appear quickly, but it cannot fake a trail of unique, countersigned tasks. Duplicate shells stall because they share traces and fail independent attestations, so the bond is slashed and the cheap replication path is closed.
